documents.title: Lung doctor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Forgot to tell you I saw the lung specialist back in November. They did the breathing tests and an x-ray and said everything was normal and I don't need to go back. My unit wants something in writing from you that I'm good.

documents.title: RE: Lung doctor
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news. We never got their letter, so we'll ask for it Monday and I'll do your paperwork as soon as it's in.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request to outside pulmonology for 11/19/25 consult note and PFT report. Their office says it was signed but never routed to us.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation (received)
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY MEDICINE CLINIC — CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 11/19/2025
Referred by: primary care, for lung function after ARDS.

Thank you for sending this 22-year-old active-duty soldier, seen about 11 weeks after an ICU admission for ARDS following a submersion event in late August (intubated, prone ventilation, extubated day 5). Earlier this year he had a laparotomy for an abdominal gunshot wound. He reports no shortness of breath, cough or exercise limitation; he has resumed running. Never smoker.
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.

Exam: well-appearing, unlabored. SpO2 98% on room air at rest and with a hallway walk. Lungs clear throughout. Heart regular. No clubbing or edema.

Chest radiograph today: clear lungs.
PFTs today: spirometry normal, DLCO normal.

Impression: full recovery of lung function after drowning-associated ARDS.
Plan: no pulmonary follow-up needed; return as needed. He may resume full duty from a pulmonary standpoint.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pulm letter from 11/19 arrived after our request. Normal PFTs and CXR, cleared. ARDS marked resolved. Duty clearance letter written and sent to pt through the portal.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23 y/o for his yearly. Rough 2025: abdominal GSW with hemorrhagic shock in March (ex lap), then ARDS after a near-drowning in August. Both fully recovered; pulm cleared him with normal PFTs. Back on full duty since January and running 5 miles again. No complaints today.
Meds: none. NKDA. Never smoker. Drinks 1-2 a week.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight back to baseline. Well-appearing. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen: well-healed midline scar, no hernia, nontender. Skin otherwise clear. Extremities and neuro normal.

A/P
- Well adult. Lipids and CBC today.
- Surgical hx: ex lap 2025. Problem list: no active problems.
- PHQ-9 2, AUDIT-C 2. Discussed how the past year has been; he says he is doing well and has people to talk to.
- Up to date on vaccines; flu next fall.
See in a year.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: August, cholesterol and blood counts are normal. Your hemoglobin is right where it was before last year. See you next spring.

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Bilateral diffuse infiltrates. Heart size normal. No pneumothorax. No displaced rib fracture. No pleural effusion.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Fractures of the pelvic ring with an unstable pattern; pelvic binder in place. Liver, spleen, kidneys and pancreas without injury. No free intraperitoneal air. Postsurgical change of prior midline laparotomy. Bladder intact.
reports.conclusion: Unstable pelvic ring fracture. No solid-organ injury.

reports.text: No intracranial hemorrhage or mass effect. No skull fracture. Ventricles and sulci normal.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: In the hospital again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, typing from my phone in the hospital. Car crash Friday night, broke my pelvis and they said fat got into my lungs. Was in the ICU on oxygen but out now. They fixed the pelvis yesterday. Not sure when I go home. Just letting you know.

documents.title: RE: In the hospital again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling us, August. Glad you're out of the ICU. We'll get the records. When they discharge you, message us and we'll see you within the week.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT — PHYSICIAN DOCUMENTATION
Date of service: 07/24/2026, 21:12

CC: Pelvic pain and shortness of breath after highway-speed MVC.

HPI: 23-year-old male driver brought in after a high-speed collision, complaining of severe pain in the pelvis and difficulty breathing. Past history of abdominal gunshot wound with laparotomy (2025) and ARDS after submersion (2025), both recovered. Takes no medications.
Allergies: NKDA. Social: never smoker, occasional alcohol, active-duty Army.

Exam: BP 100/60, HR 110, RR 28, SpO2 89% on room air. Anxious and confused, not fully oriented. Pelvis unstable to gentle compression; binder applied. Crackles in both lungs. Petechiae across the chest and in both axillae. Healed midline abdominal scar.

ABG: PaO2 60 mmHg. Hgb 12.4.
CXR: bilateral diffuse infiltrates.
CT head: negative. CT abdomen/pelvis: unstable pelvic ring fracture, no solid-organ injury.

Impression: fat embolism syndrome with hypoxemia; unstable pelvic ring fracture.
Plan: high-flow oxygen, trauma ICU, orthopedic surgery for fixation.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED record in from 7/24: MVC, unstable pelvic fracture, fat embolism syndrome. Still inpatient per his message. Will update the chart at the post-discharge visit when the summary comes.

documents.title: Fill Notification
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fill history shows 2 new Rxs filled 8/4 from the hospital: enoxaparin 40 mg/0.4 mL syringes, daily x 28 days, and oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325, #20. No discharge paperwork received yet. Flagged for RN call.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt, discharged yesterday afternoon after pelvic fixation. Using a walker, toe-touch only on the injured side per ortho. Doing his own enoxaparin shots, nurse taught him in the hospital. Breathing fine, no chest pain, confusion gone. Pain 4/10, oxycodone at night only. Has no discharge papers with him except the med list, which matches the fills. Booked with PCP Fri 8/7. Discharge summary requested from the hospital.

medications.drug_text: enoxaparin sodium 40 MG in 0.4 ML Prefilled Syringe
medications.sig: Inject 40 mg under the skin once daily for 4 weeks

medications.drug: acetaminophen 325 MG / oxycodone hydrochloride 5 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for severe pain

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23M, third major trauma admission in 17 months. 7/24-8/4 admission elsewhere after a high-speed MVC: unstable pelvic ring fracture and fat embolism syndrome (hypoxemia, confusion, petechial rash). ED record reviewed. ICU on high-flow O2, never intubated. Pelvic fixation 7/27 per pt. Discharge summary not here yet.

Now: walker, toe-touch weight bearing on the injured side. Pain 4/10, worst getting in and out of the car; oxycodone/APAP at bedtime most nights. Enoxaparin daily, no missed doses, some bruising at the injection sites. Breathing normal. No chest pain, no leg swelling. Thinking clear; says the confusion lasted a couple of days. Rash gone. On convalescent leave.

Exam: vitals as charted, SpO2 97% RA, weight down 4 kg since March. Alert, oriented x3, appropriate. Skin: no petechiae; small bruises on abdomen at injection sites. Lungs clear throughout. Heart regular, no murmur. Calves soft and nontender, no asymmetry. Pelvic incisions not examined, dressings clean and dry per pt, ortho managing.

A/P
1. Fat embolism syndrome, improving; lungs and mentation back to normal today. Adding to problem list.
2. Unstable pelvic ring fracture s/p fixation. Enoxaparin 40 mg daily x 4 wk from discharge (through about 9/1) and oxycodone/APAP prn added as outside meds. Ortho owns weight bearing and the hardware.
3. Post-hemorrhage anemia check: CBC/BMP today.
4. PHQ-9 4. Talked about three bad injuries in a row; he wants to focus on rehab for now.
5. Discharge summary requested again.
RTC 4 wk.

documents.title: Lab Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 11.7, a bit low after the injury and surgery, expected. Platelets fine on enoxaparin. Kidney function normal. Will recheck at the next visit.
